native-remote-help.stdout:
usage: omo remote <command> [--json]
  status                                   the device service's connection state
  devices                                  the devices on this account
  sessions [--device D] [--project P] [--state running|idle|ended]
                                           sessions across the account's devices
  enable | disable                         turn remote sessions on or off for this device
  control [on|off]                         whether your other signed-in devices can view and command this
                                           device's sessions (on unless you turn it off)
  wake [on|off|default]                    whether sessions on this device that are not running may be started
                                           by a message from your other signed-in devices; on unless turned off
  bootstrap                                set up this device's service for your sign-in (every omo start runs it)
  attach <session>                         open a session in the terminal UI; also takes <device>/<session>
  open <device> [--project P] [--model provider/id] [--thinking LEVEL] [--permission-preset MODE]
       [--worktree [--branch B] [--base REF]] [--prompt TEXT [--steer|--follow-up]]
                                           start a session on another device; prints <device>/<session>; it runs
                                           in MODE (default: this device's own setting, else full-access), on the
                                           model and thinking level given (a model it cannot run opens nothing),
                                           in a new git worktree of P with --worktree, and is handed TEXT first
  send <session> <text> [--steer|--follow-up] [--no-wait]
                                           send a message and print the answer as it arrives (--steer: into the
                                           running turn; --no-wait: return once the session took it).
                                           Use the thread value from open --json, or <device>/<session>.
  model <session> <provider/id>            switch the model; also takes <device>/<session>
  interrupt <session>                      stop the running turn; also takes <device>/<session>
  close <session> [--force]                end the session; --force also drops messages it has not read
